doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The State of the Global Climate is an annual WMO flagship report.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: It updates key observed indicators and presents selected high-impact events.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: It is produced with National Meteorological and Hydrological Services, data centres, research institutions and UN partners.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The 2025 edition adds a new indicator, Earth’s energy imbalance.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: It includes a case study on climate and heat impacts on health.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: It gives no projections or forecasts and prescribes no policy actions.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: CO₂ in 2024 was 423.9 ppm, 152% of the pre-industrial level.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Global temperature in 2025 was 1.43 °C above the 1850–1900 average.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: 2025 was the second or third warmest year in the 176-year record.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Ocean heat content in 2025 was the highest in the 66-year record.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Sea level at the end of 2025 was about 11 cm above January 1993.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The Arctic sea-ice maximum was 14.19 million km², the lowest on record.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Earth’s energy imbalance in 2025 was the highest since records began in 1960.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: CO₂, CH₄ and N₂O all hit record levels in 2024, the latest year with consolidated figures.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: CO₂ was 423.9 ± 0.2 ppm, 3.5 ppm more than 2023, and 152% of the 1750 level.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The 2024 CO₂ rise was the largest since modern measurements began in 1957.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: CH₄ reached 1,942 ppb, 266% of the pre-industrial level.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: N₂O reached 338.0 ppb, 125% of the pre-industrial level.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: CO₂ is the highest in at least 2 million years; CH₄ and N₂O in at least 800,000 years.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Station data show all three gases kept rising in 2025.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The 2025 temperature is 1.43 ± 0.13 °C, based on nine datasets.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: 2025 was second in two datasets and third in seven.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: 2024 remains the warmest year at 1.55 °C.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: 2015–2025 were the eleven warmest years, and 2023–2025 the three warmest in all nine datasets.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: 2025 was cooler than 2024 partly because a strong El Niño gave way to a weak La Niña.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: January 2025 was the warmest January on record.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: 2025 was the warmest year without El Niño conditions on record.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: One year above 1.5 °C (such as 2024) does not mean the Paris 1.5 °C level is exceeded, because the goal refers to decades.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: About 91% of excess energy goes to the ocean, 5% to the continents, 3% to ice, 1% to the atmosphere.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Upper-2,000 m ocean heat content set a record in 2025, and each of the past nine years was a record.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The 2005–2025 ocean warming rate is more than twice the 1960–2005 rate.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: About 90% of the ocean surface had a marine heatwave in 2025.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The ocean absorbed about 29% of human CO₂ emissions in 2015–2024.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: This lowers ocean pH (acidification).

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Ocean surface pH changed by −0.017 per decade over 1985–2025.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Eight of the ten most negative glacier mass balances since 1950 occurred since 2016.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The Arctic maximum of 14.19 million km² was on 20 or 21 March.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The Antarctic minimum of 2.06 million km² tied for second lowest.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The past four years had the four lowest Antarctic minima.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Sea level was about 11 cm above January 1993, when satellite records began.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Sea level rose 2.65 mm/yr in 1993–2011 and 4.75 mm/yr in 2012–2025.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Earth’s energy imbalance is energy received from the Sun minus energy radiated back to space.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The imbalance’s rate of increase (estimated from ocean heat content) was 0.13 W m⁻² per decade over 1960–2025 and 0.30 over 2001–2025.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Heat stored on Earth is not only increasing but accelerating.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The Texas floods on 4–5 July caused 135 deaths.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: The California wildfires in January caused 30+ deaths and over US$60 billion in losses.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Hurricane Melissa hit western Jamaica on 28 October with winds of 298 km/h.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Japan recorded 41.8 °C at Isesaki on 5 August, its highest on record.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Monsoon flooding caused over 1,000 deaths in Pakistan.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: About half the world is at risk of dengue, with 100–400 million infections a year and record reported cases.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Over a third of the global workforce (about 1.2 billion) is exposed to workplace heat risk each year.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Greenhouse gases, ocean heat, sea level and the energy imbalance were at or near record levels, while glaciers and sea ice kept losing ice.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: 2025 was among the three warmest years, and 2023–2025 are the three warmest.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Many figures refer to 2024 because consolidated 2025 greenhouse gas figures are not yet available.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Section 2: CO₂ in 2024 was “6.2 ppm more than in 2023”.
notes: PDF says 3.5 ppm more than in 2023.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Section 5: “six of the ten most negative annual mass balances since 1950 have occurred since 2016”.
notes: PDF says eight of the ten.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Section 7: Texas floods on 4–5 July caused “235 deaths”.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Section 5: “The Greenland ice sheet lost about 270 billion tonnes of ice in 2025.”
notes: PDF says only that the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets lost significant mass. It gives no tonnage and no 2025 figure.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Section 7: Pakistan’s monsoon flooding “destroyed about 2 million homes”.
notes: PDF gives over 1,000 deaths, 1.57 million people affected and over 40,000 displaced. It says nothing about homes destroyed.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Section 3: 2025 was cooler than 2024 “because” a strong El Niño gave way to weak La Niña (the word “partly” was removed).
notes: PDF says “due in part to” the El Niño to La Niña transition and “consistent with” the shift. It does not say this was the sole cause.

doc: Report 2 – WMO State of the Global Climate 2025
claim: Section 7: Hurricane Melissa had winds of 298 km/h, “the most intense landfall on record”.
notes: PDF says “equal-most intense landfall on record for a North Atlantic storm”. The claim drops “equal-most” and “North Atlantic”, so it can be read as an all-basin record.
